clue.text: Barman's one whiskey in bed

indicators.note: the whiskey letter goes in the middle of the word for a bed

parts.note: a bed of soil or rock is a layer
W is Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pub barman knocks back a whisky while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a pub worker but a member of the Bar, the body of courtroom advocates.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone called to the Bar practises law, so a barman in this sense is a legal professional.

clue.text: Fan left several balls at Old Trafford

parts.note: Old Trafford hosts cricket, where an over is a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A supporter walked out after many balls were bowled at the Manchester ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is both Manchester United's football ground and a cricket ground; the football sense misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of something is an enthusiast or devotee, someone who loves it.

clue.text: Remake of Gone with the Wind missing name in flyer

indicators.note: a remake reworks the film, so the letters of the title words are rearranged
one letter for name is left out of the title words

explanation.surface: A remake of the classic film Gone with the Wind drops a name from the cast of a flying scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the' only link the film title; 'missing' drops an N, leaving GOEWIND, which 'Remake of' rearranges. A widgeon (or wigeon) is a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigeon is a dabbling duck, and ducks are birds that fly.

clue.text: More than one approach is charming

definitions.meaning: ways in, doors or gates by which one approaches a place
delights or enchants someone, a third-person verb

explanation.surface: Several ways of coming at something prove delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun plural means ways in and the verb means holds spellbound, two words spelt alike but said differently.

clue.text: Popular female worker's recent delivery?

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
a worker is an ant, the worker caste of the colony; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A well-liked woman employee's latest piece of work, as if from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'delivery' means a birth, not a parcel or a job handed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby is what a mother has just been delivered of, so a recent arrival from the maternity ward.

clue.text: Some of them are proper novices, possibly grasping nothing

indicators.note: the novices word holds the zero letter inside it

parts.note: novices in a convent may be nuns
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Some young convent novices, perhaps, are very prim and seize on nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proper' is grammatical: proper words naming particular people or places, like London.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar classes words naming particular things as proper, so some naming words are of this type.

clue.text: Ukrainian plane not repaired in a month

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside 'a month'

parts.note: NOV is short for November

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Ukrainian aircraft still not fixed in a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircraft maker from Kyiv builds transport planes, including the giant Mriya.

clue.text: Cheap cosmetic surgeries, suppliers of 10s?

definitions.meaning: read as tummy-..., outlets selling nips and tucks cheaply
10 is the boy at school; British school snack shops sell him sweets and buns

explanation.surface: Budget clinics for facelifts are also where pupils buy their treats.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck shop is a British school snack shop; tuck is slang for sweets and cakes, and a tuck is also a cosmetic operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops selling tucks would be cosmetic clinics, while the real snack shops serve the pupils of 10-down.

clue.text: Recording it within a year shows enthusiasm

indicators.note: the recording and 'it' sit inside the letters for 'a year'

parts.note: a vid is a video recording

explanation.surface: Making a video of something within twelve months shows how keen you are.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidity is eagerness or keenness, a near synonym of enthusiasm.

clue.text: He tries way to cut fuel

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a way cuts into the word for fuel, splitting it

parts.note: juice is slang for fuel, petrol or electricity
ST, for street, is a common abbreviation for a way

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a route that will save on petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: A justice is a judge, and judges try cases, so 'He tries' defines the answer; 'tries' is not about attempting.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice is a judge or magistrate, someone who presides over and decides court cases.

clue.text: He's in form, bolshy, mostly cool, unruly

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A rebellious, mostly calm, wayward person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is a British school class, so a pupil is 'in form'; 'mostly' trims cool to COO before 'unruly' mixes it with BOLSHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a class at a British school, so a boy pupil is someone in a form.

clue.text: Roast, singe and carve beef and grouse, say

indicators.note: to roast is to cook, and cooking reworks the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction for cooking and serving beef and game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef and grouse' look like a menu, but both are slang for complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef and grouse are both informal words for a complaint, so they are examples of grumbles held against someone.

clue.text: Prominent feature larger than normal in Tyneside

indicators.note: the outsize abbreviation is put inside the letters for Tyneside

parts.note: Tyneside, the area round Newcastle, is in the North East of England, NE
OS stands for outsize, larger than the usual clothing size

explanation.surface: Some landmark in the Newcastle area stands out as unusually big.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ in the middle of the face sticks out and is often called a prominent feature.

clue.text: Latin American, for one, abandons his Twitter

indicators.note: the word 'his' is dropped from the front of the longer word

parts.note: a Latin American is an example of someone Hispanic

explanation.surface: A man from Latin America quits his social media account.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitter looks like the social network, but it is the old word for a flustered state, as in 'all of a twitter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitter is a state of nervous agitation, the same flurry of alarm the answer names.

clue.text: Dial John during function, getting silly old Venetian

parts.note: dial and pan are both slang for the face

indicators.note: the John word goes inside the function word

parts.note: tan, the tangent, is a trigonometric function
john and loo are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Phoning John at a party gets you a foolish old man from Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantaloon is the foolish old Venetian merchant of the commedia dell'arte.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italian comedy the stock figure is a doddering, foolish old Venetian.

clue.text: Old British hero housed six in blackout

indicators.note: the hero word holds the Roman numeral inside it

parts.note: a brave person is called a lion
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A veteran British war hero sheltered six people during the wartime blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime blackout fits the surface, but here it means a loss of consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing out into unconsciousness is a blackout, a state of forgetting or nothingness.

clue.text: Editorial about current priest and interpreter

indicators.note: the editorial word goes round the current and priest letters

parts.note: a newspaper editorial is a leader
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial about a modern priest who also translates.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads speech from lip movements is interpreting what is said.

clue.text: Client resolves to retain extra floor

indicators.note: the two words keep the answer held inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: A customer decides to keep an additional storey in the building.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a mezzanine, a low additional storey between two main ones.

clue.text: Remains on team controlling United

parts.note: RE means on or concerning

indicators.note: the team word holds the United letter, as if in its control

parts.note: a side is a team
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: Staying in a team that is in charge of Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb (stays) but is a noun: what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is the leftover part, what is left behind after the rest is gone.

clue.text: Stone art in the Louvre makes whistling noises

parts.note: a pip is the stone or seed of a fruit
in French, the language of the Louvre, 'tu es' means 'thou art', so art is ES

explanation.surface: A stone sculpture in the Paris museum emits a whistling sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old form of 'are' (thou art), and the Louvre points to French, where that is 'es'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds and kettles pipe when they make a high shrill whistling sound.

clue.text: Saw dog restrained by lead

indicators.note: the dog is held inside the lead symbol, as on a leash

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a classic name for a dog

explanation.surface: Someone saw a dog held back on its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun here, an old saying; 'lead' is the metal, not a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a pithy piece of folk wisdom.

clue.text: Spotted spades and other tools

parts.note: to have spotted something is to have seen it
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Someone noticed garden spades and other implements in the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' makes sense because spades are tools too: the answer names different tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothed cutting blades for wood or metal are tools, distinct from the spades already named.

clue.text: Depot uses hooter indiscriminately

indicators.note: used without care or order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A depot's staff sound the horn far too freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse, a building where goods are kept and stocked.

clue.text: Part of play watched on phone

indicators.note: heard over a telephone line, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: something watched has been seen

explanation.surface: Someone viewed a section of a drama on a mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of a drama divide into scenes, each a section of the action.

clue.text: Theatre mounts English pieces

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting climbs upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun, also called a piece

explanation.surface: A playhouse puts on English plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounts' looks like staging a play but reverses: E plus GATS read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage is the theatre as a profession, as in a career on the boards.

clue.text: Ant perhaps, small, more mature, bites one

indicators.note: the word for more mature takes the numeral between its teeth

parts.note: someone more mature is older
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A little insect, older than the rest, bites someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In many colonies a caste of large-jawed defenders exists, so a defending ant is an example of this kind.

clue.text: Notice Spanish royal installing new organ

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper

indicators.note: the Spanish word takes the letter for new inside it

parts.note: real is Spanish for royal, as in Real Madrid

explanation.surface: An announcement says a Spanish king is fitting a new church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The glands sitting atop the kidneys are endocrine organs that produce hormones such as cortisol.

clue.text: Wanted: leading pair of network journalists

parts.note: the first two letters of network are N and E
two editors, each ED, are journalists

explanation.surface: A job advert seeking the two top journalists of a broadcasting network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanted:' reads like the heading of a job ad, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wanted is required, a straight synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: He sings quavers, one of them lacking focus

indicators.note: the focus is the centre, so the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a quaver is a tremble, so one of the quavers is a single tremble

explanation.surface: A singer warbles quavers, one note blurred and unfocused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quavers' suggests musical notes, but it means shakes of the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy with a high unbroken voice in a choir is a singer of the top part.
